commit.message:
Link soreness to the workout that caused it

Soreness entries were keyed by date alone, with no reference to the workout
that caused them, so there was no way to see how long a session's soreness
actually lasted.

An entry is now identified by (date, source workout), and you log against the
same workout repeatedly as it fades — that sequence is its recovery curve.
Two workouts' soreness can overlap on the same day without fighting over one
record. Unattributed entries keep the bare `soreness-<date>` id the old scheme
used, so existing entries carry over as "unattributed" with no migration.

- Log soreness from a workout in the History feed and in the workout editor
- Soreness editor picks the originating workout first, which filters the
  muscle picker to that day's groups (with a "show all" escape hatch)
- New Lanes view: a vertical date rail where each workout spawns a stripe
  running for as long as its soreness lasted. Lanes are packed greedily by
  start date and never reflow — interval-graph colouring already gives the
  minimum lane count, so shifting a live stripe would buy no width while
  destroying the stable x-position that makes its length readable.
  Grouping, missed-day handling, order, quiet-day collapsing and the date
  window are all toggles.

Snapshot schema gains id and source_workout_* columns; the committed
snapshot.db is migrated in place so anonymous visitors keep working before
the next cron regeneration.

DELETE /api/soreness/:date becomes /api/soreness/:id, back-compatible since
a bare date still resolves to the unattributed entry.

Merge remote-tracking branch 'origin/main' into claude/soreness-workout-connection-c8732f
